definition: To register on arrival at a hotel or airport.
business_context_example: Guests can check in from 2 pm, earlier if the room is ready.

definition: To pay and leave at the end of a stay.
business_context_example: Please check out by 11, or ask about a late checkout.

definition: An arrangement to keep a room or table for someone.
business_context_example: I have a reservation under the name Petrova, for two nights.

definition: The code that identifies a reservation.
business_context_example: Could you give me your booking reference, please?

definition: A guest who arrives without a reservation.
business_context_example: We keep two rooms for walk-ins on weekdays.

definition: A guest who books but never arrives.
business_context_example: No-shows are charged for the first night.

definition: Having no rooms or tables available.
business_context_example: We're fully booked all weekend because of the festival.

definition: Having taken more bookings than there is space for.
business_context_example: The hotel was overbooked, so they moved us to a partner property.

definition: To move a guest to a better room or class of service.
business_context_example: We upgraded them to a sea view as an apology.

definition: Given free of charge.
business_context_example: Breakfast is complimentary for members of the loyalty programme.

definition: Extra facilities and items provided for guests' comfort.
business_context_example: The amenities include a gym, a sauna and a small pool.

definition: The department that cleans and prepares rooms.
business_context_example: Housekeeping starts on the top floor at 9 am.

definition: Food and drink brought to a guest's room.
business_context_example: Room service stops at midnight, except for cold snacks.

definition: Preparing a room for the night, usually in the evening.
business_context_example: Turndown service is offered in suites only.

definition: A rate including breakfast and one other meal.
business_context_example: Half board is 30 euro more per person per night.

definition: A rate including all three meals.
business_context_example: Families usually prefer full board in the summer.

definition: A rate covering meals, drinks and most activities.
business_context_example: The all-inclusive package covers everything except the spa.

definition: Several services sold together at one price.
business_context_example: The package deal includes flights, transfers and five nights.

definition: The busiest time of year, when prices are highest.
business_context_example: July and August are peak season on the coast.

definition: The quiet time of year, when prices are lower.
business_context_example: We renovate in the off season, usually November.

definition: The percentage of rooms that are filled.
business_context_example: Occupancy rate hit 92% last August.

definition: A hotel employee who helps guests with bookings and information.
business_context_example: Ask the concierge to book the restaurant, they know everyone.

definition: The parts of a business that guests see and the staff who work there.
business_context_example: Front of house needs three more people for the summer.

definition: The kitchen and areas guests don't see.
business_context_example: Back of house was calm, which is rare on a Saturday.

definition: The number of meals served or guests seated in a restaurant.
business_context_example: We did 140 covers on Saturday night.

definition: To write down what a customer wants to eat or drink.
business_context_example: Take the drinks order first, then give them time with the menu.

definition: Special food needs, for health, religion or choice.
business_context_example: Please tell us about any dietary requirements when you book.

definition: A harmful reaction to a particular food or substance.
business_context_example: A nut allergy goes on the ticket in red, always.

definition: To divide the cost between several people.
business_context_example: Would you like to split the bill or pay together?

definition: An amount added to the bill for service.
business_context_example: A 10% service charge is included for groups over eight.

definition: The final chance to order before closing.
business_context_example: Last orders at half past eleven, please.

definition: A guest telling you something was wrong.
business_context_example: Every guest complaint gets a reply within 24 hours.

definition: A polite phrase used when something has gone wrong.
business_context_example: We apologise for the inconvenience and have moved you to room 402.

definition: To give something to make up for a problem.
business_context_example: We compensated them with a free dinner and a late checkout.

definition: A document giving the holder a discount or free service.
business_context_example: Here's a voucher for two complimentary drinks at the bar.

definition: Money returned to a customer.
business_context_example: We issued a full refund for the second night.

definition: Items left behind by guests.
business_context_example: Lost property keeps everything for three months.

definition: A scheme rewarding customers who return.
business_context_example: Ten nights in the loyalty programme earns a free weekend.

definition: A detailed plan of a trip.
business_context_example: The itinerary has two free afternoons in Rome.

definition: A visit led by someone who explains what you see.
business_context_example: The guided tour of the old town takes 90 minutes.

definition: Visiting interesting places as a tourist.
business_context_example: They spent the first day sightseeing and the second at the beach.

definition: A famous building or place that is easy to recognise.
business_context_example: The cathedral is the landmark everyone photographs.

definition: Transport arranged between the airport and the hotel.
business_context_example: The transfer takes 40 minutes and is included in the price.

definition: The document allowing you to get on a plane.
business_context_example: Have your boarding pass and passport ready at the gate.

definition: A break between flights during a journey.
business_context_example: There's a four-hour layover in Vienna.

definition: Tiredness caused by travelling across time zones.
business_context_example: Give them a day for jet lag before the first meeting.

definition: Needing a lot of attention and effort to keep happy.
business_context_example: That group is high maintenance, so put your best waiter on them.

phrase: go the extra mile for a guest
definition: To do more than expected to make a guest happy.
business_context_example: She went the extra mile and found them a pharmacy at midnight.

definition: The busiest hours of the day.
business_context_example: We need four people on the bar at peak times.

definition: Workers hired only for the busy period.
business_context_example: We recruit seasonal staff every April for the summer.
